<h1>Pattern rotation</h1>

The LaunchControl's **left** and **right** arrows rotate a trig pattern: every
trig moves one step left or right, and the one that falls off the end wraps
round to the other side. The trigs you wrote are not changed. Rotation is an
offset the MSEQ applies as the pattern plays, so you can always rotate back.

Hold **SHIFT + MUTE** and press either arrow to reset the rotation, which puts
the pattern back where you wrote it. Hold **SHIFT + SOLO** and press either
arrow to randomise it.

On a **synth sequencer** the arrows rotate the whole pattern, every row
together. They work in any view except IO and peer IO, where the same arrows
page through the catalog. In a view that does not show trigs you will not see
the pattern move, but you will hear it. The jam keyboard is the one exception:
there the arrows rotate the jam keyboard's own pattern (see
[Jam keyboard](/documentation/MSEQ/jam-keyboard)).

On the **TR-8 drum sequencer** (13) the arrows rotate one row at a time, so you
can shift a single voice against the others. They act on the selected row, the
last row you pressed with 8B in the trig view, in whichever bank (main or alt)
is showing, and reset and randomise act on that row only. Boom-tsk is left
alone: while it is playing, row 1 does not rotate.
